page.layout: One page of running text, one column. Dates in the left margin, beside lines 3, 7, 9 and 12 of the text.

main_text.p: Reipublicæ est declaratus: inque ejus locum à Senatu suffecti Maximus & Albinus.

STAURATIUS à Nicephoro patre in Imperii societatem adscitus; eo defuncto, ob corporis deformitatem, ingenii stoliditatem, & turpem libidinem, à Senatu Constantinopolitano Imperio dejectus, monachum profiteri est coactus.811[?]

ROMANUS DIOGENES maximâ suorum clade à Turcis captus, ab illis tamen honorificè habitus atque dimissus: cum domi bellum denuò pararet: à Senatu captus, oculisque privatus, in insulam Proten est relegatus.1071.

ANDRONICUS COMNENUS, lupinâ sævitiâ nulli fecundus, ALEXIO agnato & pupillo perfidè strangulato, Imperium invaserat: & quò tyrannidem stabiliret, brevi quoque proceres omnes, quorum suspectam virtutem habebat, trucidarat. Bello itaque à Guilielmo Siciliæ Regè, impuberis Alexii cædem vindicaturo, undique pressus: ab ISACIO ANGE-LO, quem ad supplicium jam destinârat, præter suam omniumque opinionem ab Imperio dejectus, captusque, & altera manu oculisque mutilatus, asinæ præposterè impositus; capite aliorum reste loco diadematis præcincto, bestiæque cauda manibus pro sceptro alligatâ, spectaculum factus mundi, turbæ tandem tumultu lacer periit.1183.1185.

Pari modo Romano-Germanico Imperio dejectum fuisse legimus WENCESLAUM, quià à patre Carolo IV. successor in Imperio dictus, cunctis quidem Electorum, at multò precio coemtis & extortis suffragiis: cum per ignaviam & socordiâ Imperii res miserè afflixisset: pas-sus sibi eripi regalia jura Ducatus præsertim Mediolanensis: præsentique rerum statu contentus, nec præ-terita corrigere, nec futura præcavere curaret: adeoque ingenio esset hebete, stolido & sordido; animo verò non tantùm à Republicâ, sed penè ab omni honestate alieno, & ad immanitatem usque sævo ac tru-culento; corpore denique ignavo, vino tantum & Ve-neri

page.notes: The left-margin dates are small and partly worn. "811[?]" is a doubtful reading of the first marginal figure; the others (1071, 1183, 1185) are clearer. "esset" is read from "effet" and may be a printing error or misreading of long s; check against the scan. The page ends mid-sentence at "Ve-neri", so the paragraph continues on the next page. The page number "102" is at the head and is worn, so the reading is uncertain.
